name: Durable, replayable event streams
summary: An ordered, replicated log of events that many independent consumers read at their own pace, and can read again from any point.
body: In an event stream, producers append events to a log and nothing is deleted when a consumer reads them. Each consumer keeps its own position, so a billing service, a search indexer and a nightly batch job can all read the same events, and a new service or a fixed bug can rewind and reprocess history. Events with the same key go to the same partition and are read in the order they were written; the log is replicated across machines so a failed broker loses nothing.

To tell whether a system really handles it, check how long it can keep data and what that costs (broker disks or object storage), whether it orders events per key or per partition, what happens to ordering when you add partitions, and what delivery guarantee consumers get: at least once is common, exactly once needs transactions or idempotent writes. Compatibility with the Kafka protocol also matters, since most connectors and stream processors speak it.
